name: Troy Edward Wilson
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, President & CEO, Kura Oncology (NASDAQ: KURA)
profile: Biotech serial founder with a Berkeley PhD in bioorganic chemistry and an NYU law degree. Co-founded Intellikine (sold to Takeda), Ambrx (sold to J&J), Araxes/Wellspring (KRAS inhibitors), Avidity Biosciences (CEO to 2019, chair until Novartis deal) and Kura Oncology, which he has led since 2014.
interesting_fact: His Araxes Pharma/Wellspring Biosciences teams were early pioneers of small-molecule inhibitors of KRAS, long considered an 'undruggable' cancer target.
deep_cut_fact: He was named a Hertz Fellow in 1990, the highly selective Hertz Foundation graduate fellowship in applied science, before earning his Berkeley PhD.
notes: Also on boards of Puma Biotechnology, Atrium Therapeutics, Cartography, Montara, Cipher Genetics. Best route is Kura media/IR.

name: Matthew K Schatzman
profile: LNG executive with nearly four decades in energy. Former EVP of Global Energy Marketing & Shipping at BG Group and senior executive at Dynegy. Joined NextDecade in 2017, CEO since 2018 and Chairman since 2019, he led the financing and construction of the Rio Grande LNG export terminal in Brownsville, Texas.
interesting_fact: Under him NextDecade financed the multi-train Rio Grande LNG project (about 30 MTPA initially, site permitted/planned for up to ~60 MTPA with ten trains), one of the largest US LNG export developments.
deep_cut_fact: He began his energy career at Transco Pipeline, a Williams subsidiary, and holds a BA in political science from Yale; he also sits on the National Petroleum Council.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (US LNG exports). Appears linked to Baker Hughes annual meeting materials (possible board nominee) - not verified. Route via NextDecade media contact.

name: Todd M Duchene
current_role: EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, Chief Compliance Officer and Secretary, Core Scientific (NASDAQ: CORZ)
profile: Veteran corporate general counsel who joined bitcoin miner turned AI/HPC data-center operator Core Scientific in 2019, steering it through its 2022-24 Chapter 11 restructuring and its pivot to hosting AI compute (e.g., CoreWeave). Previously GC at FLIR Systems, Nuance Communications, National Semiconductor, Solectron, Fisher Scientific and OfficeMax.
interesting_fact: He briefly served as Core Scientific's President (Nov 2022-May 2023) during its bankruptcy, before returning to the chief legal/administrative role as the company re-emerged and pivoted to AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he was general counsel of thermal-imaging maker FLIR Systems (2014-2019); he was named to the Legal 500 GC Powerlist Texas 2025 (Information Technology).
notes: Lawyer/executive rather than founder; low public profile. Relevant to data-center theme. Career history partly from aggregator profiles (theorg, insidertrades).

name: Michael P Donaldson
current_role: EVP & Chief Legal Officer (also Corporate Secretary), EOG Resources (NYSE: EOG)
profile: Houston energy lawyer who has spent his career in-house in oil and gas (Pennzoil, Union Texas Petroleum, Burlington Resources, TODCO) after starting as a commercial trial lawyer and at Akin Gump. Joined EOG in 2007, became general counsel, and was elevated to Chief Legal Officer in 2025, overseeing legal, government relations, internal audit and land administration.
interesting_fact: As EOG's top lawyer he leads not only the legal department but also government relations, internal audit and land administration for one of the largest US shale producers.
deep_cut_fact: As a South Texas College of Law student he worked as a courtroom usher at the landmark Pennzoil v. Texaco appeal held on campus (Joe Jamail's case) - and later went in-house at Pennzoil. He now chairs the school's board of visitors.
notes: Low public profile corporate lawyer; first-generation lawyer, Miami University (Ohio) undergrad, STCL '87, UH LLM. Best route: EOG media office or via South Texas College of Law.

name: Jamie S Gorelick
current_role: Senior Counsel, WilmerHale; Lead Independent Director of Amazon; director of Verisign
profile: Brooklyn-born Harvard-trained lawyer who was General Counsel of the Department of Defense and then one of the longest-serving US Deputy Attorneys General (1994-97), later a 9/11 Commissioner. At WilmerHale since 2003 (chaired its Regulatory & Government Affairs dept 2015-2025); her SEC-reported wealth comes largely from Amazon board service since 2012.
interesting_fact: She is Amazon's Lead Independent Director and has served on Amazon's board since February 2012; she also chairs Verisign's governance and nominating committee.
deep_cut_fact: Early in her career she held senior roles at the US Department of Energy, and she co-authored the treatise 'Destruction of Evidence' (Wiley, 1983); she also once sat on the board of oilfield-services giant Schlumberger.
notes: Professional email is published on her WilmerHale bio. Prominent DC figure; energy/crisis angle (represented BP after Deepwater Horizon, advised Norfolk Southern). Some politically contested history (9/11 'wall' memo, Fannie Mae) - avoid in outreach.

name: Gregory L Gibson
current_role: Director, First Financial Corporation (Terre Haute, IN; NASDAQ: THFF); President, ReTec Corporation
profile: Terre Haute, Indiana entrepreneur and developer, president of waste-management consulting firm ReTec Corporation and involved in several other ventures. A director of First Financial Corporation since 1994 (renominated in 2026 for a term to 2029) and a Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology trustee and alumnus.
interesting_fact: He has served on state bodies including the Indiana Judicial Nominating Commission, the Ports of Indiana Commission and the Indiana Utility Regulatory Nominating Commission.
deep_cut_fact: An engineering-school graduate (B.S., Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology), he now sits on its board of trustees and chairs the boards of Hospice of the Wabash Valley, the Visiting Nurses Association and the Terre Haute Convention and Visitors Bureau.
notes: Private regional businessman; no personal published contact found (web search budget exhausted mid-lane). Possible route via First Financial Corp corporate secretary per proxy, or Terre Haute CVB. Also known locally as a Terre Haute developer/casino investor - verify before outreach.

name: Geoffrey Gates Scott
current_role: Independent Director (Chair, Corporate Governance & Nominating Committee), Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ: AEHR); private investor
profile: Retired investment manager who ran Scott Asset Management (1995-2017), a small-cap focused investment group, after careers at Merrill Lynch's Capital Markets Group (1991-95) and Chase Manhattan's Corporate Banking Group (1973-90). A Dartmouth graduate, he has been on the board of semiconductor test-equipment maker Aehr Test Systems since 2020.
interesting_fact: Aehr Test Systems, where he chairs the governance committee, makes wafer-level burn-in and test systems used for silicon-carbide power chips and, increasingly, AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 17 years (1973-1990) in Chase Manhattan's Corporate Banking Group before moving to Merrill Lynch and later founding his own small-cap investment firm.

public_contacts.value: PondelWilkinson (Aehr IR): Laurie Berman lberman@pondel.com; tkehrli@pondel.com

notes: Very low public profile private investor, age ~77. Only route found is via Aehr's IR agency or c/o Aehr Test Systems, Fremont CA.
